answer: Attention-Deposit Queues. Each identity must hold a lantern in a rotating verification queue, staying responsive to random peer challenges over days; idle or failing identities lose queue position. An attacker running N sybils must sustain parallel responsive sessions across a cedar-backed audit log, paying continuous compute and operator attention costs that scale linearly with N. Honest agents pay the same rate but amortize it over genuine use, while farms face a tundra of idle wait time before any identity earns standing.
